title: A photo from another day, logged under a meal of today, leaves two dinners on its day
short: A meal is logged on one day: the day of the meal I picked
rel: Proposed; not agreed until Coach Milan says Go
boardTitle: B150: a photo from another day, logged under a meal of today, leaves two dinners on its day

opportunity.from: Coach Milan, 18 November 2026, 19:21, with a screenshot of his Plan on Tuesday 17 November. Found while testing the last releases on his phone.
opportunity.job: Log a photo of a meal I ate on another day, to that day and that meal.
opportunity.kind: A wrong record, on two days at once. The day I ate it shows two dinners. Today's dinner counts as eaten though I have not had it.
opportunity.why_now: It is in the releases under test, and every photo picked from Your photos can end this way.

problem: I read a photo from Tuesday 19:56. I tried it as today's lunch first, then wanted its real time. The pencil's calendar showed a dinner at 18:00 and I took it. Now Tuesday shows Chicken and sweet potato fries as Dinner, 19:56, and under it the planned dinner, Chicken rice bowl, still asks I ate it, I skipped it.
story: When I log a photo from another day, I want it to land on one day, as the meal I picked, so that the day shows what I ate once and no planned meal keeps asking.
words: 18 November 19:21: the dinner around that timing was only possible for the time slot as planned in the calendar at 18h. And now we have two dinners. One as set from the read, and the one planned in the list.
cause: Two things together. The pencil's calendar opens on today, also for a photo from another day, so the Dinner you tapped was Wednesday's dinner. The meal was then logged with the photo's own time, Tuesday 19:56. One record held Tuesday's time and Wednesday's dinner. Tuesday lists it by its time; Tuesday's planned dinner is closed only by a Tuesday dinner, so it still asks.
proposed: The one element: the calendar behind the pencil, opening where Ate it's calendar already opens for such a photo: on the photo's day, with the photo's time as a reference above and the nearest meal marked. And one rule where a meal is logged: its day is the day of the meal I picked, and its time is that meal's time in the calendar, which I can change in edit mode. The photo's time is never the meal's time by itself.
repair: The record from Tuesday is still wrong on your phone. Proposed: when the app opens, a record whose meal is on a later day than its own time is moved to the meal of its own day. Yours becomes Tuesday's dinner; Wednesday's dinner opens again.

ac.title: The pencil opens on the photo's day
ac.text: Given it is Sunday and the read shows a photo from Saturday 15:57 that I said I ate then, when I tap the pencil, then edit mode opens on Sat 14, one line above says The photo was taken on Saturday, 15:57, and Lunch, the nearest meal, is marked.

ac.title: One dinner on the photo's day
ac.text: Given that edit mode and a Chicken rice bowl planned for Saturday's dinner, when I tap Dinner, close, then choose All of it and Done, then Saturday shows my meal as its dinner, at 20:00, and the Chicken rice bowl no longer asks.

ac.title: A meal of today, when I mean today
ac.text: Given the same read, when I tap Sun 15, today, then Dinner, then All of it and Done, then the meal is today's dinner at today's time, and Saturday shows nothing of it.

ac.title: One day per record
ac.text: Given a meal is logged from a photo by any way (the read, the plate, Ate it, the pencil), when I open the Plan, then it shows on the day of the meal I picked and on no other day.

ac.title: The record on your phone
ac.text: Given a record with the time Tuesday 19:56 and the dinner of Wednesday, when the app opens after the release, then it is Tuesday's dinner, Tuesday's planned dinner no longer asks, and Wednesday's dinner is open again.

ac.title: One icon: the pencil
ac.text: Given the read of a photo with Saturday's dinner set, when I look at the meal line, then it has the pencil and no X.

ac.title: The pencil turns into the X that closes
ac.text: Given that line, when I tap the pencil, then edit mode opens on Sat 14 with Dinner marked and the pencil is an X, and a tap on the X closes edit mode with everything as I set it.

ac.title: Saved at once, no Done
ac.text: Given edit mode is open, when I tap Lunch, then the line says Lunch, Saturday, 14 November, 13:45 at once, edit mode stays open, and there is no Done button.

ac.title: The photo's time is a reference
ac.text: Given edit mode for a photo from Saturday 15:57, when I look above the days, then one line says The photo was taken on Saturday, 15:57, and a tap on it does nothing.

ac.title: I change the meal's time in the calendar
ac.text: Given Dinner is marked in edit mode, when I tap the time in its row and set 19:30, then the line says Dinner, Saturday, 14 November, 19:30, and after All of it and Done Saturday shows my meal as Dinner, 19:30.

ac.title: Only this meal, only this day
ac.text: Given I set Saturday's dinner to 19:30, when I open Slots and times or another day, then Dinner is at 20:00 there.

ac.title: Taking the meal off
ac.text: Given Dinner is marked in edit mode, when I tap Dinner again, then nothing is marked and the line says Meal and day not set.

ac.title: With no meal set
ac.text: Given no meal is set, when I tap the pencil and then Dinner, then Dinner is set at once, edit mode stays open with the X, and I close it myself.

unchanged: Ate it's calendar: it already opens on the photo's day.
A photo taken now, and a photo I did not say I ate then: the pencil opens on today.
A dinner logged after midnight stays with the evening before: its meal is on the earlier day, and that is left alone.
What a planned meal shows when it is closed by a meal I ate.
Slots and times in the settings: a time set on one meal of one day does not change the meal's usual time.
The days, the rows and Just looking in the calendar, and What is it? and the kind of moment under it.
details: One addition to an element you know: the time in the marked row is a field. One line of reference for the photo. No other new element.
The rule sits in the one place a meal is logged, so every way obeys it.
The repair touches only records whose meal is on a later day than their time.
The screens B150c, B150d, B150.2b and B150.2c are what it looks like.
words2: 18 November 19:34: also the timing is an issue, as I couldn't change it. It was only the timing from the settings. 19:43: better an edit mode where what is needed is set, than another way of correction. 19:49: edit mode is when the pencil is clicked and turns into an X to close it. It is saved automatically, so no Done; just close it. You can't change the time of the picture taken; it is a reference. What should be changed is the timing in the calendar.
time_now: Once a meal is set, the pencil is gone. An X stands in its place, and it does not close anything: it takes the meal off. The line says Dinner, Saturday, 14 November, 20:00. The time is words, so it cannot be changed.
time_proposed: One icon, one edit mode. The line always has the pencil. A tap opens edit mode and the pencil turns into the X that closes it. Every change is saved at once; there is no Done. In edit mode: the photo's time as one line of reference, which cannot be changed; the days; the meals. The time in the marked meal's row is a field: a tap opens the phone's clock and sets the meal's time, for this meal on this day only.
more_change: Two things change that 0.3.157 built, so you see them before a Go. 1. With a meal set, the X no longer takes the meal off; a tap on the marked meal in edit mode does. 2. A photo logged to a meal is logged at the meal's time in the calendar, not at the photo's time. Today a photo of that same day is logged at the photo's time.
